identity.real_world_identity_notes: Lotus 72E, the final development of the Lotus 72 raced from 1973 to 1975, running the Ford Cosworth DFV on a Hewland FG400 five-speed manual.

wheel_rim.notes: Observed from the cockpit during the guided drive.

notes: Simulator behaviour was directly observed in a guided drive in AMS2 1.6.9.91 with automatic clutch and shifting disabled. There is no automatic cut or blip, so the driver lifts to upshift and blips to downshift.

The gearbox is a racing Hewland, engaged by dog rings rather than synchronisers, so the driver must match revs on a downshift for the gear to engage cleanly. The downshift blip is therefore required. Dog-ring construction is inferred from Hewland's design approach rather than stated by the source, and a source showing a synchronised FG400 would make the blip optional.

This class reports a single aero configuration. The selection screen offers no high or low downforce package, and only the plain identity has ever been observed, so there is no further identity to carry.
Observed live in AMS2 1.6.9.91 via guided verification observation ams2.lotus-72e.20260815t192559098z-8bad4fbd by Jason Kinslow.

confidence.basis: Simulator behaviour was live-tested in AMS2 1.6.9.91 with automatic clutch and shifting disabled, and the real-world transmission is supported by registered sources.

claims.basis: A registered source establishes the car and its Hewland gearbox, and the exact simulator identity was observed live.
The source names a Hewland FG400, and the live drive selected five H-pattern gears with no automatic cut or blip.

The registered source names a Hewland FG400 but does not state how it engages. Dog-ring construction is inferred from Hewland's design approach rather than stated by a reviewed source, so this value is medium confidence: a source showing the gearbox was synchronised would change it, and would make the downshift blip optional.
Directly observed during the guided drive: move-off, shift clutch use, automatic cut and blip, and the cockpit rim.

driver_summary: Hewland FG400, most likely a dog box, so blip every downshift to be safe. Whether the gear needs it was never tested, and the dog-ring construction is inferred from Hewland's practice rather than named by a source.
